# VAR Select

```{r}
## create a new data frame with differenced variables

daseas = cbind(dseasAQI,dseasPM25,dseasPM10, dseasNO2,dseasCO, dseasSO2, dseasO3)

vseseas = VARselect(y=daseas,lag.max = 8, type="none") #no constant/time trend based on ?


crit = vseseas$criteria

seq = c(1:3)
seqs = c(1:8)
crit1 = matrix(NA, 3, 8,
            dimnames = list(c("AIC", "HQC","SIC"), paste("Lag ", seqs, 
                                                        sep ="")))
for (i in seq){
  for (j in seqs){
    crit1[which(seq==i),which(seqs==j)] = crit[i,j]
  }
}

kable(round(crit1,3), caption = "Model Selection Criteria for Lags")

```



```{r}
#identifying the optimal lag length, selection based on criteria
selseas  = matrix(NA, 3, 1,
            dimnames = list(c("AIC", "HQ","SIC"), paste("Lag", 
                                                        sep ="")))
sel = round(vseseas$selection,3) #tells you which one has the smallest from each model selection
for (i in seq){
  selseas[which(seq==i)] = sel[i]
}
kable(selseas, caption = "Optimal Lag Lengths") #SIC is more parsimonious while AIC likes larger models better. 

```

AIC says 20 lags are optimal, but SIC and HQC say 1 lag. We will go with 20.

```{r}
library(vars)
p = 2 #optimal lag based on previous question 
#run reduced form VAR with lag length = p, and w/o a constant
va = vars::VAR(daseas,p=p,lag.max = 8,type="none")
summary(va)

p2 = 7 #optimal lag based on previous question 
va2 = vars::VAR(daseas,p=7,lag.max =8,type="none")
summary(va2)
```



```{r}
bmat = diag(7) #question specifies 4x4. If this was not given, we would use the number of betas in the equation. This is the number of variables included in the equation. If there are 4 vars, then 4x4. Takes away the covariation between the variables.

diag(bmat) = 1

#define the diagonal and create our NA values in the matrix
#Identify the NAs we plan to solve for
# for setting up the Bmatrix: upper diagonal is all 0, lower diagonal is all NAs, diagonal is all NA.
bmat[2,1] = NA
bmat[3,1:2] = NA
bmat[4,1:3] = NA
bmat[5,1:4] = NA
bmat[6,1:5] = NA
bmat[7,1:6] = NA


#Next we solve for the system to get our NA values for the #B-matrix
#SVAR command to run regression to solve unknowns
#we use the reduced form results/data
#estimation type is direct
#then we specify our A-matrix and B-matrix
#warning bc number of meqns is = to the # of unknowns, so we cannot perform testing
# reg = SVAR(va, estmethod = 'direct', Amat = NULL, Bmat = bmat)
reg = vars::SVAR(va,estmethod = "direct",Amat = NULL, Bmat=bmat)
  #estmethod is determined by the Bmatrix. If we do it with NA assigned instead of random, then we are doing recursive identification which is direct. Lecture 9, Slide 13-15.

  #estmethod is determined by the Bmatrix. If we do it with NAs random, then we are doing non-recursive identification which is direct. Lecture 9 Slide 16

#Amatrix: we don't need to do this but look at the lecture also

#Lecture 9, slide 25-29: recursive restrictions/identification example

kable(round(reg$B, 3))

```

```{r}
vasum <- summary(va)
vacovres = vasum$covres
causality(va, cause = "dseasCO")
vacovres
vacovres%*%t(vacovres)

```


p-value is almost 0, so we reject the null hypothesis, so there is instantaneous causality between at least one of the other variables and the AQI. That was expected.

# Historical Decomposition

```{r 1b}

N = ncol(daseas)
nam = colnames(daseas)

#Step 1: first obtain companion form. First obtain structural shocks using regression from the b matrix.

#Step 1a
B = reg$B #obtain our B matrix from the structural VAR model

#Step 1b. residuals from data set from VAR using updated da data using optimal lag length
u = residuals(va) #obtain the residuals from the reduced form model

#Step 1c. transpose B matrix and multiply by residuals
w = solve(B)%*%t(u) #calculate the structural shocks as 
                    #B inverse times our residual
w = t(w)

### Step 2: Next calculate thetas. Obtain companion form with 2 lags. Lags were specified in the VAR. N is the number of columns in the data set.  companion form is similar to B matrix, but we are interested in lags rather than number of vars.

## if we were interested in 2 lags, we would do 2x2. 6 lags, 6x6

B = reg$B #obtain our B matrix from the structural VAR model
u = residuals(va) #obtain the residuals from the reduced form model
w = solve(B)%*%t(u) #calculate the structural shocks as 
                    #B inverse times our residual
w = t(w)

### Next calculate thetas
#first obtain companion form

a = Bcoef(va) #va is the var model we specified earlier. dimensions is number of columns times number of variables to determine dimensions of the matrix. 3 vars, 4 lags = 12 rows, 12 cols
a
I = diag(N) # N is number of columns of the da dataset (number of variables)
oh = matrix(0,N,N)
```

```{r}
## creates a list to generate list of A from 0 to t-1
An.list = list()
An.list[[1]] = as.matrix(An)
TT = length(w[,1])

for (j in 1:(TT-1)){
  An.list[[j+1]] = An.list[[j]]%*%An.list[[1]]
}

## In this case Theta 1 is the Cholesky decomp.
###create list of thetas
THETA = list()

## generate theta_0 values
## if you need to do Cholesky with a matrix that is smaller than the Cholesky, multiply by Identity matrix then you can multiply by Cholesky.

THETA[[1]] = B
    ## Next we create the loop to calculate all THETAS up to T-1
for (i in 1:(TT-1)) {
  THETA[[i+1]] = (J%*%An.list[[i]]%*%t(J))%*%THETA[[1]]
}

NAME = colnames(daseas)

# Historical Decomposition
tg = 1 
```

```{r}
##PLOTTING HISTORICAL DECOMP
yhat = matrix(NA, TT, 7, dimnames = 
              list(c(), c("Shock1", "Shock2", "Shock3", "Shock4", "Shock 5", "Shock 6", "Shock 7")))

tg = 1

## calculate the first time period manually
tt = 1
yhat[tt,] = THETA[[1]][tg,]%*%diag(w[tt,]) #do all 4 shocks at once


##calculate all 4 shocks at once for all remaining time periods

###storing all of the shocks from the yhats across all of the first periods. Slide 15 of Lecture 10
for (tt in 2:TT){
  jy = THETA[[1]][tg,]%*%diag(w[tt,]) #do all 4 shocks at once
  for (i in 1:(tt-1)){
    jy = jy + THETA[[i+1]][tg,]%*%diag(w[(tt-i),]) #do all 4 shocks at once
  }
  yhat[tt,] = jy
}
#sums all rows of each yhat
yyhat = rowSums(yhat) ## all contributions of shocks at each time point. All 4 shocks combined at each point in time to movements of Y_t
yhat2 = yhat[,-c(dseasCO)]

```
